questions.prompt: You're about to export your tree as an audio file. What's the right thing to check FIRST?

options.label: Listen to the read-aloud once and rewrite any line where the voice felt wrong — the audio file freezes the reading.
Add five more lines so the audio file is longer.
Change every character's voice register to match the system voice.

questions.mentorPostScript: Export is a freeze. Listen first; revise; THEN export.

questions.prompt: The audio file is shared via AirDrop / Files / Messages. The tree's title becomes the filename. What rule does the title need to follow?

options.label: Letters, numbers, spaces, dashes, and underscores — anything else gets replaced so the filename stays clean.

questions.mentorPostScript: Clean filenames travel. Untidy ones land in the trash.

questions.prompt: The audio export ends on the LAST line of one branch — but the tree has two branches. What's the most honest export choice?

options.label: Walk the tree depth-first so every branch gets read aloud, in order — the listener hears both paths.
Pick the longer branch and skip the shorter one.
Pick the kid's favorite branch and skip the rest.

questions.mentorPostScript: Branching dialogue means TWO paths matter. The audio should respect that.

questions.prompt: The audio file is on your device only — it doesn't leave unless you share it. Why does that matter?

options.label: Your character voices, the title, the lines — none of it lands on a server somewhere. You decide what travels.
The file is smaller because it never connects to a network.
Apple speeds up local files for you.

questions.mentorPostScript: On-device means the kid owns the voice. That's a craft choice AND a kindness.

questions.prompt: After you export, the audio file is in the share sheet. Where's a good place to send it?

options.label: A grown-up's device — for them to hear what you've been writing.
A stranger's phone number from a chat app.
Anywhere on the internet — it's a fun thing to share.

questions.mentorPostScript: Share with grown-ups you trust. Your characters are yours; they travel where you say.
